prompt: Talk trash on behalf of the U.S. Navy about the Battle of Midway. Four carriers in five minutes. Rub it in.
response:
You want me to channel the spirit of a swaggering, swabbie-talking, World War II naval aviator? Say no more. Stow your gear and listen up, because we're about to rub some salt in a wound that’s been festering since June 4th, 1942.

*(Cue the sound of a radial engine roaring to life and .50 caliber shells clattering into a hopper)*

"You want to talk about the Battle of Midway? The 'Miracle at Midway'? Please. Don't insult us by calling it a miracle. A miracle is something you pray for. What we did was pure, surgical, high-octane vengeance, delivered by the best damn pilots on the face of the earth. You’re talking about the United States Navy turning the pride of the Imperial Japanese fleet into artificial reefs in the time it takes to brew a pot of coffee.

Five minutes. Let that sink in. In five minutes—less time than you’ll spend standing in the chow line—we erased months of their planning and decades of their so-called 'warrior spirit.' We’re talking about the Kido Butai, the iron fist that had sucker-punched Pearl Harbor and run wild across the Pacific. They thought they were invincible. They thought they were samurai. They were just targets.

Here’s the blow-by-blow, so you can feel the heat from the flight deck.

First, you had the torpedo squadrons. VT-8, VT-6, VT-3. Those guys in their slow, obsolete Devastators, flying straight into a wall of Zeros and anti-aircraft fire with nothing but guts and a prayer. They got massacred. They didn’t score a single hit, and don’t you ever forget their sacrifice. They dragged the Japanese combat air patrol down to the deck, right where we wanted them.

And then, from 20,000 feet, out of the sun, here come the big boys. The SBD Dauntlesses of VB-6 and VS-6 from the *Enterprise*, and VB-3 from the *Yorktown*. Wade McClusky, Dick Best—remember those names, because they’re the ones who signed the death warrants. The Zeros were down low, swatting at the torpedo planes. The decks of the *Akagi*, *Kaga*, and *Soryu* were chaos—planes, fuel hoses, and bombs strewn everywhere, a perfect tinderbox just begging for a spark.

And we did more than spark it. We lit them up like the Fourth of July.

Dick Best put a single, 1,000-pound bomb right through the middle of the *Akagi’s* rising sun. One bomb. That’s all it took to turn their flagship into a floating crematorium. The *Kaga* took four hits and looked like a volcano erupting. The *Soryu* got blasted so bad her own crew couldn’t recognize her. Three carriers, ablaze from stem to stern, knocked out of the war in the span of a single watch.

But we weren’t done. Oh no, we believe in finishing the job. Later that afternoon, we found their last flattop, the *Hiryū*. She was the one that had hit the *Yorktown*, and she was feeling pretty proud of herself. That pride lasted exactly as long as it took a strike from the *Enterprise* to find her. We put four bombs into her forward elevator and turned her into a bonfire so big you could probably see it from Tokyo. Four carriers. Four. The entire heart of their naval aviation, sent to the bottom by guys who had been flying combat for maybe six months.

So let’s review the tally. You came looking for a decisive battle. You got one. You lost four fleet carriers, 248 aircraft, and over 3,000 of your best, most irreplaceable pilots and mechanics. We lost one carrier, the *Yorktown*, which, by the way, you had to sink three times because she just wouldn’t quit. We traded a single carrier for four of yours. In carrier warfare, that’s not a victory. That’s a going-out-of-business sale.

Midway wasn’t a miracle. It was a beatdown. It was the moment the rising sun hit its zenith and immediately went into a nose-dive. You thought you were the hunters? You sailed right into an ambush and found out the hard way that the U.S. Navy doesn’t just hit back. We hit harder, faster, and with a hell of a lot more style.

So go ahead, tell the story of the invincible Kido Butai. We’ll be here, polishing our Navy Crosses with a piece of a Zero’s wing, remembering the day we proved that five minutes is all it takes to change the world. Now get out of my ready room. We’ve got a war to win."
